hypotheses.primary: At equal encoded bytes, retaining X dependence improves prediction of a fixed target-conditional teacher over independent X plus the same predictor, when the teacher, residual law, support, precision, sample size and random streams are held constant.
alternatives: Any apparent gain is finite-sample variation across generated source families.
The target mechanism or inductive bias, rather than X dependence, explains the difference.
Optimization or quantization changes effective capacity despite equal encoded byte budgets.
The teacher is not representable by one or more candidate families at the frozen budget.

design.byte_accounting: canonical encoded artifact bytes including all sampling dependencies; reject over-budget cells

source_holdouts.rule: generated mechanisms are split by source seed before fitting; rows from one source seed never cross partitions

model_holdouts.rule: teacher families are frozen before candidate fitting; held-out teacher cells are descriptive validity checks only

design.teacher: same frozen target-conditional function and intercept in every X-dependence arm
design.residual_law: same homoscedastic Gaussian residual draw per row and seed in every arm
design.support: same ordered feature support in every arm
design.varied_factor: X dependence only: independent marginals versus fixed correlated-X copula; full-joint candidates also model X and Y jointly
design.stop_rule: Run one priced correctness pilot only. Stop if it exceeds its 2 CPU-second cap, fails exact normal-equation checks, or reports nonfinite values. Do not retry unchanged. Admit the development factorial only after the common matched-byte harness, model holdout construction, and resource quote are reviewed; unsupported cells remain in the denominator. No automatic campaign or roster expansion.

candidates.description: Independent X marginals plus the identical fixed predictor; charge predictor and sampling dependencies.
Fixed correlated X model plus the identical target predictor.
Joint X,Y generator; compare at the same complete encoded-byte cap.
Sparse oblivious-tree target with the same X and residual draws.
Sparse GA2M target with fixed interaction support budget.
No circuit target representation or sampler is implemented.
No low-rank residual target representation or sampler is implemented.
Exact float64 XTX/XTy ridge solution with lambda 1 and unpenalized intercept, checked before f32 quantization; not a privacy or generalization comparator.

cost_cap.development_price_basis: hard CPU-time cap only; development study is not admitted until a measured per-candidate price and common artifact harness are recorded

pilot.evidence: cargo test --locked --lib joint_ablation_tests -- --nocapture; 2 deterministic fixtures passed
pilot.note: The fixed two-CPU-second cap applies to pilot test execution, not one-time compilation; the command wall time is retained separately and excluded from model-fit cost.

admission_blocker: The current compiler has no shared harness that freezes the same teacher, X support, residual draws, source/model holdouts, and complete encoded-byte cap across predictor, dependence-only, joint, and target-mechanism candidates. Circuit and low-rank residual candidates are unsupported. Only the narrow ridge normal-equation control is admitted as a correctness pilot; the factorial development study remains blocked.
